strengths: Novel unsupervised approach: Learning adaptive parallel computation solely from LM loss without explicit supervision is creative and well-motivated, differentiating it from pause-token methods.
Rigorous experimental design: Fair comparisons with both parameter-matched and computation-matched baselines (Copy-N), multiple scales (150M-772M), and multiple datasets (OpenWebText, peS2o).

Strong interpretability analysis: Evidence that the method learns meaningful computation allocation—correlation with entropy (Figure 4), meaningful forked token-to-parent attention (Figure 5), and task-appropriate allocation on CLUTTR (Section C).
Consistent improvements in controlled settings: Perplexity improvements across scales and datasets demonstrate the mechanism's basic validity.
Clear mathematical formulation and reproducibility: Detailed architecture description, hyperparameters (Tables 2-3), and promised code release enable verification.
weaknesses: Critical efficiency gap: Acknowledged poor wall-clock performance despite FLOPs advantages. Only FLOPs-matched (not time-matched) comparisons provided. Custom hardware kernels needed but unimplemented. This fundamentally undermines practical utility.

Cannot evaluate on stated motivation: Main motivation is reasoning models, yet no evaluation on reasoning benchmarks (GSM8k, MATH, etc.). Authors cite scale limitations. Current tasks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag) are relatively simple, leaving core claims unvalidated.

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Recent adaptive computation methods cited (Mixture of Depths, Sun et al. 2025, Goyal et al. 2024) but not compared against. Only compared to standard transformer and naive copy-based baseline. Unclear if complexity is justified.

Unresolved technical issues: (1) Top-K gradient bottleneck—forking in later layers hurts performance; proposed fix (noise) untested. (2) Distribution shift at inference—dynamic forking still underperforms blockwise (21.18 vs 20.97 perplexity). Suggests method hasn't fully solved adaptation.

Modest and inconsistent performance gains: Perplexity improvements modest (0.7 points at 772M). BLiMP shows no improvement over computation-matched baseline (80.4 vs 81.2). PIQA shows no improvement. Some LAMBADA results show high variance (5.0 to 29.4 accuracy).

Limited ablations: Only overforking ablation provided. No ablations on fork embeddings, partial RoPE rotations, attenuation scheme, or output averaging. Many design choices (layers 3,7,11) lack justification.

Method complexity: Many design choices feel ad-hoc (partial RoPE rotation, per-layer fork embeddings, score attenuation scheme). Unclear which components are essential or how sensitive results are to design variations.

Presentation issues: Section 2.3 is dense; notation (x^(k)_{i,j}) initially confusing. The motivation for specific design choices (especially partial RoPE) not well explained. Why forking only in early layers is underspecified.

strengths: Novel unsupervised approach to learning adaptive computation during pretraining without explicit thinking tokens
Interpretable computation allocation: demonstrates model learns to allocate computation to high-entropy regions without supervision (Figure 5)
Comprehensive experimental scope across 150M-1.9B scales with detailed ablations and analysis
Competitive wall-clock efficiency while maintaining performance gains
Attention analysis effectively demonstrates forks meaningfully influence parent token computation (Figure 4)
weaknesses: Critical brittleness in learning signal: removing attention masking causes 23% performance degradation (loss 3.17→3.90, Table 7), suggesting scores don't naturally learn to be meaningful without this specific constraint—raises questions about robustness and generalizability

Efficiency claims are misleading: headline 'half token budget' compares 20B tokens (ours) vs 40B (baseline); at equal 40B tokens, results are mixed with some benchmarks worse (HellaSwag 54.16→50.04, ARC-Challenge 26.17→24.50)
Zero-shot improvements are marginal or absent: at 40B token comparison, GSM8K shows essentially no improvement (31.50 vs 31.46), LAMBADA is tied, and BLiMP/PIQA show only marginal gains
Cheap approximation (Eq. 12) replaces principled probabilistic formulation for main results, undermining theoretical elegance and unclear how this affects model capabilities

Critical design choices lack principled justification: fixed forking positions (layers 3,7,11), RoPE partial rotation scheme, and dynamic forking adjustment for autoregression appear as engineering patches rather than principled solutions

Distribution mismatch requiring mitigation: dynamic forking adjustment (Section G.1) is needed to prevent distribution shift during autoregression, suggesting fundamental limitations for different inference settings
Insufficient comparison to alternatives: doesn't convincingly demonstrate advantages over simpler methods like pause tokens or Mixture-of-Depths
Limited reasoning improvement: no advantage on GSM8K despite focus on scaling inference-time compute for complex tasks
